'''Gord Miller''' (born March 27, 1953) was the [[Environmental Commissioner of Ontario]], having served from February 1, 2000 to May 18, 2015.  He was appointed to a five-year term in 2000 and was reappointed to this position in 2005 and 2010 for two consecutive five-year terms.<ref name="toronto.ctvnews.ca">{{Cite web | url=http://toronto.ctvnews.ca/miller-reappointed-as-environmental-commissioner-1.515509 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140407194614/http://toronto.ctvnews.ca/miller-reappointed-as-environmental-commissioner-1.515509 | url-status=dead | archive-date=April 7, 2014 |title = Miller reappointed as environmental commissioner &#124; CTV News| date=25 May 2010 }}</ref>  He also ran unsuccessfully for federal and provincial office in various [[Ontario]] electoral districts.

==Early life==
Before his appointment, he worked for the Ontario Ministry of the Environment for 14 years as a scientist, manager of training and development, and as a district manager. He also helped to set up the advocacy organization Ontario Public Interest Group Guelph.<ref>{{Cite web | url=http://www.guelphmercury.com/news-story/5633563-former-ontario-environmental-commissioner-gord-miller-plans-to-run-for-green-party-in-guelph/ | title=Former Ontario Environmental Commissioner Gord Miller plans to run for Green Party in Guelph| date=2015-05-20}}</ref> Miller received an Honours [[Bachelor of Science]] degree in [[Biology]]  in 1976 and a [[Master of Science]] degree in [[Plant ecology]] in 1978, both from the University of Guelph.<ref>{{Cite web | url=http://www.therecord.com/news-story/5634509-former-ontario-environmental-commissioner-gord-miller-plans-to-run-for-green-party-in-guelph/ |title = Former Ontario environmental commissioner Gord Miller plans to run for Green Party in Guelph|date = 2015-05-19}}</ref>

==Tenure as environment commissioner==

As environment commissioner, Miller issued strongly-worded reports annually, calling the province to account on its environmental commitments. Starting in 2008, he added special reports on greenhouse gas emissions and energy conservation.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Oved|first1=Marco|title=Former Ontario environment watchdog Gord Miller to run for Green Party|url=https://www.thestar.com/news/canada/2015/05/19/former-ontario-environment-watchdog-to-run-for-green-party.html|website=thestar.com|publisher=Toronto Star Newspapers Ltd|accessdate=27 October 2015|date=19 May 2015}}</ref>

Miller did not shy away from direct criticism of government decisions and longstanding abuses in law. An early example was his direct condemnation of [[Strategic lawsuit against public participation|SLAPP]] lawsuits for their negative effect on public advocacy. Miller's reports very strongly supported "environmental activists" who argued, "the practice is widespread in the development industry and used to pacify activists and environmentalists",<ref>{{cite news|last1=Gray|first1=Jeff|title=Ontario looks to smack down SLAPPs|url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/report-on-business/industry-news/the-law-page/ontario-looks-to-smack-down-slapps/article1390137|website=theglobeandmail.com|publisher=The Globe and Mail Inc|accessdate=27 October 2015|date=23 August 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Nuisance lawsuits targeted by Ontario government|url=https://www.thestar.com/news/queenspark/2013/06/04/nuisance_lawsuits_targeted_by_ontario_government.html|first=Robert|last=Benzie|date=June 4, 2013|access-date=June 19, 2020|website=The Toronto Star}}</ref> that is, silence them with fear of civil liability. Ontario passed an anti-SLAPP law in 2010.

In 2013 Miller called to public attention the fact that Ontario’s cabinet had allocated to itself, in the 2012 budget, the power to turn over public land to the exclusive control of private, multinational corporations. In a formal report Miller said that this, combined with cuts to staff and programs at Ministries of Natural Resources and the Environment, all "quietly and without public consultation", led to a situation with "no rules". Other actions were, Miller said, "gutting" protections for species at risk and that it was time for [[hydraulic fracturing]] regulation.<ref>{{cite news|title=Ontario Liberals quietly loosened environmental rules, watchdog warns|url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/news/politics/environmental-watchdog-slams-ontario-liberals-over-cutbacks/article14795721/|first=Adrian|last=Morrow|newspaper=The Globe and Mail |date=October 10, 2013|access-date=June 19, 2020}}</ref>

In 2014 Miller warned that Ontario had done "very little" other than closing coal plants to meet its 2020 [[emissions target]]s, and had failed to build transit and other efficient infrastructure.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ontario warned it will miss 2020 emissions target|url=https://www.thestar.com/news/queenspark/2014/07/09/ontario_warned_it_will_miss_2020_greenhouse_gas_emissions_target.html|first= Richard|last=Brennan|website=[[Toronto Star]] |date=July 9, 2014|access-date=June 19, 2020}}</ref>

===Appointment controversy===
Miller's sharp turn on the Harris government ended a longstanding controversy.  Due to his two prior candidacies, Miller's initial appointment raised the perception by the NDP and Liberal caucuses that he was a Conservative partisan.  Opposition parties at Queen's Park accused the Harris government of using its majority to name a Conservative as Ontario's environment commissioner.<ref name="AppointmentOpposition">{{Cite web|url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/opposition-questions-gordon-miller-s-appointment-as-environment-commissioner-1.181173|title=Opposition questions Gordon Miller's appointment as Environment Commissioner|last=|first=|date=December 15, 1999|website=CBC News|access-date=}}</ref> Miller was subsequently re-appointed twice by two successive parliaments headed by Liberal governments,<ref name="toronto.ctvnews.ca" /> whom he sharply criticized.

==Politics==

Miller was, in addition to a former federal and provincial PC candidate, the president of the federal Conservative riding association in Nipissing, home riding of then-Premier [[Mike Harris]].<ref name="AppointmentOpposition" />

On May 19, 2015, Miller sought the [[Green Party of Canada]] nomination for the seat of [[Guelph (federal electoral district)|Guelph]] in the upcoming [[2015 Canadian federal election|Canadian federal election]],<ref>{{Cite web | url=http://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/toronto/gord-miller-to-seek-green-party-nomination-in-ontario-riding-of-guelph-1.3079298 |title = Gord Miller to seek Green Party nomination in Ontario riding of Guelph &#124; CBC News}}</ref> and on June 8, 2015, he was selected to run.<ref>{{Cite news | url=http://m.thespec.com/news-story/5667680-green-party-in-guelph-makes-it-official-elects-gord-miller-as-candidate-in-federal-election |title = Green party in Guelph makes it official, elects Gord Miller as candidate in federal election|newspaper = The Hamilton Spectator|date = 2015-06-08|last1 = Shuttleworth|first1 = Joanne}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web | url=https://greenparty.ca/en/riding/2013-35032 | title=Guelph}}</ref> He had gone to university there in 1977-79 and helped found the Ontario Public Interest Research Group in Guelph.<ref name="Mercury" />

Miller had also previously run for provincial Progressive Conservatives in 1995 and in 1997 for [[Jean Charest]]'s federal Progressive Conservatives.  He said the 2015 [[Conservative Party of Canada]] "is not like and doesn't represent the points of view" of those parties:<ref name="Mercury">{{Cite web | url=http://www.guelphmercury.com/news-story/5633563-former-ontario-environmental-commissioner-gord-miller-plans-to-run-for-green-party-in-guelph/ |title = Former Ontario Environmental Commissioner Gord Miller plans to run for Green Party in Guelph|date = 2015-05-20}}</ref> "We thought we were uniting the right, instead we united the wrong".<ref name="Mercury"/>

Miller was considered a star candidate by local media.  From his first public appearance he sharply criticized all the other parties for "committing to pursuing an economy based on bitumen from Alberta that we'll never be able to extract", echoing former [[Bank of Canada]] head [[Mark Carney]]'s formal raising of this issue at the [[Financial Stability Board]] and [[Bank of England]] in 2014.<ref>{{Cite news | url=https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2014/oct/13/mark-carney-fossil-fuel-reserves-burned-carbon-bubble |title = Mark Carney: Most fossil fuel reserves can't be burned|newspaper = The Guardian|date = 2014-10-13|last1 = Shankleman|first1 = Jessica}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web | url=http://www.huffingtonpost.ca/2014/10/16/mark-carney-carbon-bubble-bankers_n_5997420.html |title = Mark Carney Slams Bankers, Warns Most of World's Oil Can't be Burned|date = 2014-10-16}}</ref>  Miller also accused the government of "silencing" scientists and called [[Bill C-51 (41st Canadian Parliament, 2nd Session)|Bill C-51]] "a terrible piece of legislation."<ref>{{Cite web | url=http://www.guelphmercury.com/news-story/5635710-gord-miller-s-green-candidacy-could-shake-up-guelph-federal-race/ |title = Gord Miller's Green candidacy could shake up Guelph federal race|date = 2015-05-20}}</ref>
